The characters 史 (history), 吏 (government official), 使 (cause; use; instruct), and 事 (matter; work; affair) are all etymologically related and all derive from the same ancient character, depicting a hand (又) holding some object.

The characters 史 (history), 吏 (government official), 使 (cause; use; instruct), and 事 (matter; work; affair) are all etymologically related and all derive from the same ancient character, depicting a hand (又) holding some object.

Simplified form of 學.  Originally composed of the numbers five (㐅) and six (六), representing study of arithmetic. 
Later two hands (又) were added on the left and right side of the character, possibly depicting counting with fingers or hands-on teaching.

The bottom part of 六 (six) was reanalyzed as 宀 (roof) and interpreted as a building for learning.

Simplified form of 學.  Originally composed of the numbers five (㐅) and six (六), representing study of arithmetic. 
Later two hands (又) were added on the left and right side of the character, possibly depicting counting with fingers or hands-on teaching.

The bottom part of 六 (six) was reanalyzed as 宀 (roof) and interpreted as a building for learning.

en: suffix, used to form interrogative 什麼|什么[shén​me], what?, indefinite 這麼|这么[zhè​me] thus, etc
note: Variant form of 幺. In simplified Chinese 么 is also used to mean "[particle]", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 麼.
